chapter_theme: A short song at Valliyur (வள்ளியூர்): the body is an illusion like lightning at night, and the poet asks whether he must suffer along every stony road; the praise names the vel that ruined the Suras' town and Murugan between his two consorts.

635.reading: The poet calls the body an illusion, like the lightning at night and not even that, and asks whether he and his hand must suffer along every stony road. The praise names the vel that wore down the old Suras and ruined their town, and Murugan dwelling at Valliyur with his two consorts on either side.
635.nuance: அல்லில் நேரும் மின் அதுதானும் அல்லதாகிய உடல் மாயை: the body is less lasting than a flash of lightning at night. The second quatrain (கல்லின் நேர அவ்வழி தோறும் கையும் நானும் உலையலாமோ) may speak of wandering on hard roads or of begging with the hand; I cannot settle it.
